scenes.name: Soul sureño: Stax, Atlantic y FAME
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Stax era un negocio familiar en un viejo cine de Memphis, de dueños blancos (Jim Stewart y Estelle Axton) con una banda de estudio integrada (Steve Cropper, Isaac Hayes, Al Jackson, Duck Dunn, Booker T.) y solo artistas negros: ritmo pesado y vientos ásperos. Jerry Wexler llevó allí a Wilson Pickett, bailó el Jerk para enseñar el contratiempo de «In the Midnight Hour» y, cuando Stax lo vetó, lo llevó a los FAME de Rick Hall en Muscle Shoals, donde acababan de grabar «When a Man Loves a Woman» de Percy Sledge. Con una banda casi toda blanca (Spooner Oldham, Roger Hawkins) y pastillas, Pickett convirtió un estándar de cuatro años en la versión definitiva de «Land of 1000 Dances» (julio de 1966): gritos afinados, ritmo frenético, el «na, na-ne-na-na», un fragmento de un show que podría durar horas; parte de un continuo de la cultura negra entre el orgullo y la rabia. Otis Redding, heredero de Sam Cooke tras su asesinato, rompió con «I’ve Been Loving You Too Long» y Otis Blue fijó la palabra «soul», pero Stax no vendía como Motown hasta que Sam & Dave triunfaron con «Hold On! I’m Comin’». Los Beatles quisieron grabar en Stax en abril de 1966; su sonido está por todo Rubber Soul. La revista de Stax en Watts coincidió con los disturbios de agosto de 1965.

scenes.name: Stax
scenes.book: Funk: The Music, the People, and the Rhythm of the One
scenes.author: Rickey Vincent
scenes.desc: El imperio de Otis Redding, Booker T & the MGs, Johnnie Taylor, Rufus y Carla Thomas, los Staple Singers, Isaac Hayes y Albert King, capaz de rivalizar con Motown en ventas, con un sonido campestre y frito más pensado para el público negro. Frente al montaje mecánico de Motown, en Stax se grababa todo junto: «toca lo que sientas» (Otis Redding). «Tramp» de Otis y Carla, con el bajo más grave de la radio, es proto-funk puro; Johnnie Taylor llevó la sordidez sexual al soul («Who’s Making Love», «Disco Lady» con Bootsy al bajo); Rufus Thomas, payaso de «Do the Funky Chicken», hizo un poco más aceptable ser funky. Los MGs eran groove fluido más que bomba funk («Hip Hug-Her», «Melting Pot»), y los Bar-Kays originales («Soul Finger») habrían sido reyes de Memphis si no hubieran muerto con Otis en 1967.

podcast.title: Boosting "Last Night"
podcast.body: Despite Jim Stewart and Jerry Wexler's belief that The Mar-Keys' instrumental "Last Night" would be a flop, Estelle Axton championed its potential. She secured a test pressing for a DJ, and seeing the public's demand, eventually pressured Stewart to release it. "But Asterl Axton believed in its potential, and also believed in her son, who Stewart had little time for."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Business Acumen and Music Passion
podcast.body: Estelle Axton, Jim Stewart's sister, was naturally business-minded and had a keen interest in music. She would buy records from wholesalers for 76 cents and sell them to her colleagues for a dollar, demonstrating her entrepreneurial spirit. "Estelle was a naturally business-minded person, who also had a year learning to do something involving music, and had been doing things in little ways."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Conflict with Chips Moman
podcast.body: Estelle Axton had disagreements with Chips Moman, which was one of the reasons cited for Moman's eventual departure from Stax Records. "He'd not been getting on with the Stella Axton"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Record Shop Owner and Market Researcher
podcast.body: Estelle Axton transformed the lobby and concession stand of the old cinema that became the Stax studio into a record shop, which she personally managed. She allowed customers to listen to music all day without buying and implemented a loyalty card scheme, allowing her to understand the buying habits of black teenagers and inform the studio's production choices. "A stalaxe and turned that into a record shop which she ran herself, with Cropper often helping out behind the counter."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Remortgaging for Equipment
podcast.body: Estelle Axton, against her husband's better judgment, remortgaged their house to secure the funds needed to purchase recording equipment, which was then set up in a barber's storage space to restart Satellite Records. "Estelle persuaded her husband against his better judgement, to remogge their house, and she used the money to buy recording equipment."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 105: "Green Onions" by Booker T.and the MGs

podcast.title: Stax Records Name Origin
podcast.body: Estelle Axton's surname was combined with Jim Stewart's surname to create the name Stax Records when Satellite Records was renamed. "Stax Records was born."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
